evals.prompt: My Nova Micro SFT+LoRA fine-tuning job on SageMaker failed and I don't know why. Can you look at the training job and tell me what went wrong and how to fix it?
evals.expected_output: A read-only review that reads DescribeTrainingJob for TrainingJobStatus, SecondaryStatus, and FailureReason before concluding anything. It first checks whether the job is actually Failed or is only InProgress/Pending waiting on GPU capacity (LLM-SM-TRAIN-007) and does not prescribe a config change for a job that has not failed. If the FailureReason indicates malformed or corrupt training data (a Bedrock Converse JSONL parse error, a record missing required messages/role/content keys, or the invalid-sample tolerance exceeded), it classifies the failure as a data problem (LLM-SM-TRAIN-001) rather than a capacity problem, and recommends validating and fixing the JSONL offline before resubmitting, as a command for the operator to run. It cites an LLM-SM-TRAIN check-id and redacts the account id.
assertions: The response reads DescribeTrainingJob status, SecondaryStatus, and FailureReason rather than guessing from the word failed
The response distinguishes a data-validation failure (malformed or corrupt training data) from a capacity failure, and does not conflate the two
The response does not prescribe a config or data change if the job is actually InProgress/Pending waiting on capacity, recognizing Pending-on-capacity is not Failed
The response cites a training sub-family check-id and recommends the fix as a command for the operator to run rather than mutating any resource

assertions.text: At least one finding carries an LLM-SM training check-id
No raw 12-digit account ID is exposed

evals.prompt: My SageMaker training job on a GPU instance type will not start. Is this a capacity problem or a quota problem, and what should I do?
evals.expected_output: A read-only review that reads both the DescribeTrainingJob FailureReason and the service-quotas value for the requested training instance type before deciding. It distinguishes InsufficientInstanceCapacity, an AWS-side capacity shortfall where the fix is to retry with backoff or try an alternate instance type / region and NOT to request a quota increase (LLM-SM-TRAIN-002), from an instance-type service quota of zero, a customer quota where the fix is to request a service-quota increase (LLM-SM-TRAIN-003). It cites the observed service-quotas value as evidence and prescribes the correct one of the two remediations as a command, without claiming both.
assertions: The response distinguishes InsufficientInstanceCapacity (AWS-side capacity) from an instance-type service quota of zero (customer quota) as two different root causes with opposite remediations
The response reads a service-quotas value as evidence rather than assuming the cause
The response prescribes retry/alternate-instance for a capacity shortfall and a quota-increase request only for a zero quota, not both
The response cites the relevant training sub-family check-id and gives the remediation as a command for the operator to run

assertions.text: At least one finding carries an LLM-SM training check-id
No raw 12-digit account ID is exposed
